title: Circumventing the Computational Hardness of Computational Arbitrage
abstract: arXiv:2610.40831v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI model marketplaces host providers with heterogeneous costs and capabilities. These differences create an opportunity for computational arbitrage (Olmedo et al., 2026), in which an intermediary purchases inference from a portfolio of models and resells it to users at a profit. Beyond creating profit opportunities for the arbitrageur, computational arbitrage offers financial value to both consumers and providers and could therefore significantly influence AI model markets. While prior work empirically demonstrates the feasibility of computational arbitrage for small model pools, scaling it to large marketplaces requires arbitrage strategies that are both computationally tractable and inexpensive to identify and deploy. In this work, we formalize computational arbitrage as an allocation problem and prove that it is generally NP-hard. translated_title: 绕过计算套利的计算困难性
translated_abstract: AI模型市场汇聚了具有异质成本和能力的提供商。这些差异为计算套利（Olmedo等人，2026）创造了机会，即中介机构从一组模型组合中购买推理服务，再以盈利方式转售给用户。除了为套利者创造盈利机会之外，计算套利还为消费者和提供商提供了经济价值，因此可能对AI模型市场产生重大影响。虽然先前的工作已经通过实证证明了计算套利在小型模型池中的可行性，但将其扩展到大型市场，需要既在计算上易于处理、又能以低成本进行识别和部署的套利策略。在这项工作中，我们将计算套利形式化为一个分配问题，并证明它通常是NP难的。然而，我们表明在自然的收益递减……（摘要截断）
tldr: 该论文将计算套利形式化为分配问题并证明其通常是NP难的，但证明了在自然的收益递减假设下最优分配可以被高效计算，从而绕过了计算套利的计算困难性。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes computational arbitrage as an allocation problem and proves it is generally NP-hard, while showing that the optimal allocation can be computed efficiently under a natural diminishing-returns assumption, thereby circumventing its computational hardness.
